scope: Unit author hypotheses at corrected submission; independent review required

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces three components own separate rules but currently coordinate through inconsistent direct calls around one badge revocation.
items.decisiveFact: Three components own separate rules but currently choose inconsistent call orders around one badge revocation; a coordinator can standardize the sequence without guaranteeing race-free access denial.
items.nearestAlternative: A single access manager that owns every component's rules would centralize the protocol but also absorb their distinct domain responsibilities.
items.changedCondition: If only two components interacted through one stable call, a dedicated coordination object might add needless indirection.
items.identityReason: The source badge-revocation domain and visibility invariant remain; the revised decision is whether a narrow coordinator can resolve the actual multi-party call protocol.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces four separate modules participate in a fixed cross-module sequence and current peer calls form loops.
items.decisiveFact: Four separate modules participate in a fixed cross-module sequence and current peer calls form loops.
items.nearestAlternative: A label renderer can call the carrier and shipment modules, but that makes a presentation component own validation and workflow sequencing.
items.changedCondition: If label generation were a simple call to one carrier module, direct collaboration could remain clear.
items.identityReason: The source label-after-correction workflow is retained; the candidate targets its loop-producing multi-module protocol rather than generic central ownership.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces four participants have separate policies but a many-to-many interaction around one move workflow.
items.decisiveFact: Four participants have separate policies but a many-to-many interaction around one move workflow.
items.nearestAlternative: The room calendar could become the coordinator, but it does not own cancellation fees or participant notification policy.
items.changedCondition: If the calendar alone validated and stored room availability, no separate mediator would be needed for that single responsibility.
items.identityReason: The source rehearsal-room move and capacity/cancellation facts remain; the proposed decision is coordination of independently owned policies, not ownership transfer.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces three separate owners must participate in a maintenance transition, and cyclic peer calls make the sequence unclear.
items.decisiveFact: Three separate owners must participate in a maintenance transition, and cyclic peer calls make the sequence unclear.
items.nearestAlternative: The control panel can coordinate the flow, but it does not own equipment safety or technician assignment.
items.changedCondition: If one equipment module performed all three responsibilities itself, a separate collaboration object would be unnecessary.
items.identityReason: The source exhibit-maintenance domain and unsafe-command condition are retained; the proposal makes the three-party interaction order decisive.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces three modules must coordinate one retirement while progress identity remains stable and each module owns separate records.
items.decisiveFact: Three modules must coordinate one retirement while progress identity remains stable and each module owns separate records.
items.nearestAlternative: The catalog can call the progress service and curriculum service, but then every future consumer becomes another catalog dependency.
items.changedCondition: If retirement only removed one catalog entry and had no cross-module effects, a direct catalog operation would be adequate.
items.identityReason: The source lesson-retirement and stable-progress facts remain; this version focuses on the circular coordination among modules.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces three consumers react to one close operation after a final revision is frozen, and peer-initiated calls form a cycle.
items.decisiveFact: Three consumers react to one close operation after a final revision is frozen, and peer-initiated calls form a cycle.
items.nearestAlternative: The exporter can call the session list and messaging modules after export, but it does not own closure or participant messaging.
items.changedCondition: If export were the only reaction to closure, a direct subject-to-export call could be enough.
items.identityReason: The source whiteboard close/export facts are retained; the new decision concerns the multi-module close protocol and frozen revision boundary.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces three separately owned modules react to one paired owner/deadline change, and a chain would make each consumer dispatch the next.
items.decisiveFact: Three separately owned modules react to one paired owner/deadline change, and a chain would make each consumer dispatch the next.
items.nearestAlternative: The queue can notify messaging and monitoring, but it would become a coordinator for modules outside its ownership.
items.changedCondition: If only the queue record changed and no consumers depended on it, direct update would be enough.
items.identityReason: The source escalation's owner/deadline invariant remains; the revised decision is the narrow boundary for coordinating its separate reactions.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces a listing owner validates two prerequisites before coordinating three separately owned publication effects.
items.decisiveFact: A listing owner validates two prerequisites before coordinating three separately owned publication effects.
items.nearestAlternative: The search index can trigger the other updates after indexing, but it does not own seller messaging or market feeds.
items.changedCondition: If the listing only needed a single search-index write, a direct call would remain simpler.
items.identityReason: The source produce-listing validity facts are retained; the proposal focuses on coordinating prerequisite validation and separate publication consumers.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces three modules coordinate one split, and all must use one original identity and delivery promise.
items.decisiveFact: Three modules coordinate one split, and all must use one original identity and delivery promise.
items.nearestAlternative: The vendor-message module can tell the customer-status module when each vendor responds, but it would own another team's delivery view.
items.changedCondition: If only vendor notification followed a split, no mediator would be needed for a single outgoing message.
items.identityReason: The source parts-split identity and promise are retained; the new case focuses on coordination among its three independent participants.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces three modules participate in an approved transfer, while plot boundary and approval history must remain one shared change.
items.decisiveFact: Three modules participate in an approved transfer, while plot boundary and approval history must remain one shared change.
items.nearestAlternative: The allocation board can call the other two, but then it must understand directory and audit APIs beyond its reservation role.
items.changedCondition: If the board were the only record affected by transfer, a direct operation would be adequate.
items.identityReason: The source plot transfer and approval-history invariants remain; the proposal focuses on breaking direct links among the three owners.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces four independently owned operations must run in a defined order to create one regional bundle.
items.decisiveFact: Four independently owned operations must run in a defined order to create one regional bundle.
items.nearestAlternative: The billing module can trigger setup and catalog checks, but billing does not own entitlement or catalog policy.
items.changedCondition: If the bundle were only one catalog record with no other effects, a mediator would not be warranted.
items.identityReason: The source regional bundle and component pricing invariant remain; the candidate makes the actual four-party protocol the decision.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces four participants coordinate one reservation and adding a consumer currently changes several peer relationships.
items.decisiveFact: Four participants coordinate one reservation and adding a consumer currently changes several peer relationships.
items.nearestAlternative: The reservation store could call all consumers, but then it must own operator and grid communication protocols.
items.changedCondition: If the only follow-up were one stable update to the grid schedule, direct calls could be simpler.
items.identityReason: The source capacity/expiry reservation case remains; the proposal tests the concrete many-peer coordination cost when adding a consumer.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces three modules depend on one accepted metadata revision but must retain separate data ownership.
items.decisiveFact: Three modules depend on one accepted metadata revision but must retain separate data ownership.
items.nearestAlternative: Search can update catalog and rights checks after indexing, but search does not own either peer's data or validation rule.
items.changedCondition: If only the catalog were affected, a direct metadata method would be enough.
items.identityReason: The source metadata merge and stable asset identity remain; the new decision targets the direct peer graph around a shared revision.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces four modules need one exact approved territory/expiry, while each retains a distinct responsibility.
items.decisiveFact: Four modules need one exact approved territory/expiry, while each retains a distinct responsibility.
items.nearestAlternative: The notification module can fan out the decision, but it should not become the owner of rights evaluation or catalog updates.
items.changedCondition: If the approval only updated a single rights record, a direct rights-service call could suffice.
items.identityReason: The source territory/expiration case remains; this revision concerns routing its unchanged approved scope across four owners.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces three owners participate in one replacement flow and their current direct references form a cycle.
items.decisiveFact: Three owners participate in one replacement flow and their current direct references form a cycle.
items.nearestAlternative: The availability board can initiate the replacement because it shows free batteries, but it does not own fleet allocation or maintenance history.
items.changedCondition: If the operation only changed one assignment record, a direct allocation-service call would be sufficient.
items.identityReason: The source battery-assignment uniqueness case is retained; the candidate targets the cyclic collaboration rather than redefining which battery is valid.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces four owners collaborate on one consent-bound route and the current call loops obscure its named recipient.
items.decisiveFact: Four owners collaborate on one consent-bound route and the current call loops obscure its named recipient.
items.nearestAlternative: The audit module can coordinate routing because it records decisions, but it does not own consent or external transmission.
items.changedCondition: If the navigator alone checked consent and sent the referral, direct calls could remain simpler.
items.identityReason: The source referral privacy and consent boundary remain; the revised decision is where to coordinate its four distinct owners without changing recipient authority.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces one completion with fixed version references triggers two independently owned updates, without making the tracker know their storage.
items.decisiveFact: One completion with fixed version references triggers two independently owned updates, without making the tracker know their storage.
items.nearestAlternative: The progress view can call analytics after saving its state, but it would make one consumer dispatch another and may pass a different version.
items.changedCondition: If the tracker owned both outputs, direct sequencing within it could be simpler.
items.identityReason: The source exercise-version and score-policy facts remain; the candidate focuses on a narrow cross-module completion protocol.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces two independent approval owners decide one attributed request, and a rejection must keep it pending without merging their records.
items.decisiveFact: Two independent approval owners decide one attributed request, and a rejection must keep it pending without merging their records.
items.nearestAlternative: Compliance can call budget control, but it would become the dispatcher for a peer whose decision it does not own.
items.changedCondition: If one team owned both controls and the same record, a direct local workflow could be appropriate.
items.identityReason: The source procurement exception's actor/rationale/control facts remain; the proposal focuses on coordination between its separate approval owners.
